# Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

> Reviewed by `/plan-ceo-review` on 2026-09-10, mode HOLD SCOPE (user-selected).
> Original plan content is preserved below. Accepted amendments are marked
> `[AMENDED Dn]` and reference the decision registry in the review record.

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key
  single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters.

`[AMENDED D4, D5, D9]` The original sketch (read-through fill, delete-on-write,
"no additional coordination between a cache fill and a write") violates the
read-after-write contract above (finding F1). The ordering rules below replace
it. "Write completes" means `writeProfile` settles for its caller.

```javascript
// inflight: existing per-key single-flight wrapper, extended with
//   run(key, fn)        -> joins or creates entry {promise, stale:false}
//   invalidate(key)     -> entry.stale = true; detach entry so later callers start fresh
// cache: existing LRU adapter; get() maps the absent-sentinel back to null (D3)
async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!flag.cacheEnabled(key)) return repository.read(key);      // same bucket fn as writes (D9)
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  return inflight.run(key, async (entry) => {
    const value = await repository.read(key);                    // typed errors propagate; entry released
    if (!entry.stale) cache.set(key, value);                     // D4: skip fill if a write committed meanwhile
    return value;
  });
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  try {
    return await repository.write(key, update);
  } finally {
    inflight.invalidate(key);   // D4: in-flight fills for this key must not land
    cache.delete(key);          // D5/D9: always, regardless of outcome or flag bucket
  }
}
```

`[AMENDED D3]` The repository's absent result is `null`. The adapter maps
`null` to the absent sentinel on `set` and back to `null` on `get`; the wrapper
never sees the sentinel and `undefined` remains the only miss signal.

`[AMENDED D9]` Any change to the runtime flag value (on, off, or percentage)
resets the cache to empty. The read and write paths evaluate the same
deterministic key-to-bucket function.

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. `[AMENDED D6]` That suite also runs
against the cache-enabled wrapper on a warm cache (each case read twice).

New wrapper tests cover hit/miss, eviction and byte limits, TTL,
adapter-failure fallback, successful-write invalidation, `[AMENDED D5]`
failed-write invalidation (replaces "failed-write preservation"), and
concurrent-miss coalescing. `[AMENDED D4]` Ordering tests use a pausable
repository stub and cover both completion orders of an in-flight miss against a
write, the late-joiner case, and the absent-sentinel variant (see Section 4
schedule). `[AMENDED D9]` Flag tests cover bucket parity between reads and
writes and flush on percentage change. Oversize single values, negative caching,
and DTO mutation isolation have explicit assertions (Section 6).

The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,
then 50%, then all keys after one healthy hour at each stage. Monitor hit/miss,
eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95 without raw IDs.
`[AMENDED D7]` Read latency is recorded per path (`hit`, `miss`, `bypass`) so
the p95 target is checked against all reads and diagnosed per path.
`[AMENDED D8]` Two alerts ship with the change: cache in bypass or fallback
state for more than 5 minutes, and hit ratio below 40% for 15 minutes after a
5-minute warmup. The runbook entry is in Section 8.
On error-rate or latency regression, disable the flag immediately; both reads
and writes bypass the cache while disabled, and enabling creates an empty cache.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors
the rollout and records the results against the acceptance targets.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.

## CEO Review Record (HOLD SCOPE)

Run context: automated headless capture. System audit, environment setup,
telemetry, codebase exploration, and all shell commands were skipped by run
rules. Base branch: `main` (from git status snapshot). No design doc or handoff
note was checked (skipped audit). Every decision point below was auto-decided to
the recommended option per run rules and is recorded in the decision registry.
Outside review: disabled by `.gstack-section-state-PL5pWm/config.yaml`
(`codex_reviews: disabled`); no fallback dispatched.

### Step 0

**0A Premise.** Measured, not hypothetical: one-week trace, 900 hot keys, DB CPU
70%, p95 120 ms. A process-local cache is the most direct lever for repeated
reads in a single-process service. Doing nothing leaves the DB one traffic step
from saturation. Not a proxy problem. OK.

**0B Existing code leverage.** Reused: LRU adapter (limits, TTL, sentinel,
fallback), per-key single-flight wrapper, runtime feature flag, repository
contract tests, typed error mapping. Nothing is rebuilt. The single-flight
wrapper gains one method (`invalidate`) under D4.

**0C Dream state.**
```
  CURRENT STATE                THIS PLAN                       12-MONTH IDEAL
  repo -> DB on every read     repo <- LRU wrapper, flagged,   same repo seam; cache
  DB CPU 70%, p95 120 ms  ---> invariant-safe fills      --->  impl swappable (local or
  single process               DB CPU <50%, p95 <60 ms         distributed) w/o caller change
```
Moves toward the ideal: the seam stays at the repository interface.

**0C-bis Implementation alternatives.**
```
APPROACH A: Sketch as written (minimal)          Effort S  Risk High  Completeness 5/10
  Pros: fewest lines; reuses adapters unchanged
  Cons: violates read-after-write contract (F1); late joiners get stale snapshots;
        failed ambiguous writes leave stale entries (F2)
  Reuses: LRU adapter, single-flight, flag
APPROACH B: Sketch + in-flight invalidation (recommended)   Effort S  Risk Low  Completeness 9/10
  Pros: meets the stated invariant with a bounded structure (no per-key counters);
        one new method on an existing wrapper; smallest diff that is correct
  Cons: single-flight wrapper changes; needs ordering tests with a pausable stub
  Reuses: everything in A plus the single-flight entry as the invalidation token
APPROACH C: Write-through + in-flight invalidation (ideal-architecture candidate)
                                                  Effort M  Risk Med  Completeness 9/10
  Pros: warm entry right after a write; slightly higher hit rate on write-heavy keys
  Cons: couples the write result shape to the read DTO; same guard still required;
        hot data is read-heavy so gain is marginal
  Reuses: same as B
RECOMMENDATION: B. Right-sized diff that meets the contract; C adds coupling for
no measured benefit; A fails a stated invariant.
```
D1 auto-decided: B.

**0F Mode.** HOLD SCOPE, set by the user for this run (D2, not asked). Fits the
"iteration on existing system, correctness-critical" default. Committed: no
expansions surfaced; repairs needed to meet stated invariants are in scope.

**0D HOLD SCOPE analysis.** Complexity: about 5 files (wrapper, single-flight
wrapper, metrics/alerts config, wrapper tests, contract-suite harness). No new
services. Minimum change set equals the amended plan; nothing deferrable without
breaking an acceptance target or invariant.

**0E Temporal interrogation (resolved now).**
- Hour 1: where sentinel mapping lives (D3: adapter, not wrapper).
- Hours 2-3: how a fill knows a write intervened (D4), and what a failed write
  does to the cache (D5).
- Hours 4-5: flag bucket parity for reads and writes, and flush on percentage
  change (D9); metric label set without raw IDs (Section 8).
- Hour 6+: ordering tests need a repository stub with explicit pause/release
  points and fake timers for TTL (Section 6).
Human ~6 h / CC ~40 min.

### Section outcomes

1. **Architecture.** 1 issue: F1 (D4). Dependency graph and system diagram
   below. Coupling added: wrapper depends on single-flight entry state and flag;
   justified. Single point of failure: the one process (pre-existing). 10x load:
   1000-entry cap thrashes first (eviction metric shows it; capacity changes are
   out of HOLD scope). Rollback: flag off, seconds; code revert not needed.
2. **Error & rescue map.** 12 paths mapped, 1 GAP: F2 (D5). Registry below. No
   catch-all in the wrapper; the adapter's internal fallback must log the error
   class and increment `cache_fallback_errors_total` (existing behavior to verify).
3. **Security.** 0 issues requiring a decision. No new endpoints, params, or
   secrets. Authorization stays upstream; cache key includes tenant. Cross-tenant
   key ambiguity and warm-path authorization are verified by F3/D6. Memory bounded
   by adapter caps. No raw IDs in logs or metric labels (asserted in tests).
4. **Data flow & edge cases.** 10 edge cases mapped; 3 originally unhandled
   (F1, F2, F6), all remedied (D4, D5, D9). Async schedule below. No user-visible
   interactions (internal backend).
5. **Code quality.** 0 new decisions. Wrapper has 3 branches; fits existing
   patterns. Immutable DTO contract is verified at the cache boundary with a
   mutation-isolation test (implementation of a stated contract, no approval
   needed). Undefined-as-miss requires D3.
6. **Tests.** Test map below; 1 gap: F3 (D6). Pyramid: mostly unit, one contract
   suite integration, one trace replay. Flakiness: TTL via fake timers; ordering
   via explicit pause/release, no sleeps.
7. **Performance.** 1 issue: F4 (D7). No N+1, no new queries or indexes. Memory
   max 16 MiB plus in-flight map bounded by concurrent misses. Slowest paths:
   miss (DB p95), bypass (DB p95), hit (<1 ms). No new connections.
8. **Observability.** 1 gap: F5 (D8). Metrics: `cache_hits_total`,
   `cache_misses_total`, `cache_fill_skipped_total{reason=stale|oversize}`,
   `cache_evictions_total`, `cache_bytes`, `cache_mode` (enabled|bypass|disabled),
   `cache_fallback_errors_total`, `cache_flush_total{reason}`,
   `read_latency_seconds{path=hit|miss|bypass}`. Logs: structured, operation +
   error class, no keys. Runbook: bypass alert -> read adapter error log -> toggle
   flag off/on to reinitialize -> if it recurs within an hour, leave disabled and
   file a defect. Debuggability: a stale-read report 3 weeks later is reconstructed
   from `fill_skipped{stale}` and `flush` counters plus write timestamps.
9. **Deployment.** 1 risk: F6 (D9). No migration. Flag evaluation failure
   defaults to bypass (existing SDK default, verify). Old/new code overlap: none
   (single process, flag-gated). Post-deploy checklist: first 5 min: `cache_mode`
   enabled, fallback errors 0, hits rising; first hour: hit ratio, eviction rate,
   DB CPU trend, per-path p95, error rate within SLO. Smoke: read twice, second is
   a hit; write then read observes new value.
10. **Long-term trajectory.** Reversibility 5/5. Debt: 1 item, the in-flight
    token needs an ASCII comment in the single-flight wrapper and must be kept
    current. No path dependency; the repository seam is preserved. 1-year
    readability: good once the ordering rule is in the code comment.
11. **Design & UX.** SKIPPED, justified: no UI, API, or user-visible change.

### Diagrams

System architecture (new parts marked `*`):
```
  caller ──▶ authz ──▶ readProfile*/writeProfile* ──▶ repository ──▶ DB
                          │        │       │
                          │        │       └──▶ flag (bucket per key)
                          │        └──▶ inflight* (per-key entry {promise, stale})
                          └──▶ LRU adapter (1000 / 16 MiB / 30 s, sentinel 10 s)
                                     └──▶ metrics/logs (no raw IDs)
  Before: caller ─▶ authz ─▶ repository ─▶ DB
  After:  caller ─▶ authz ─▶ wrapper ─▶ {adapter, inflight, flag} ─▶ repository ─▶ DB
```

Data flow with shadow paths (read):
```
  key ──▶ flag? ──▶ cache.get ──▶ inflight.run ──▶ repository.read ──▶ fill? ──▶ value
   │        │          │              │                │                │
  nil/bad:  eval err:  throws:        joins existing:  typed error:     entry.stale:
  rejected  bypass +   adapter        same promise     propagate, no    skip fill,
  upstream  log        bypass +       (same gen only)  fill, release    return value
  (existing)           metric                          entry
  empty result (absent): null ──▶ adapter stores sentinel (10 s) ──▶ get returns null
  oversize value: adapter skips set, metric reason=oversize, cache stays enabled
```

Async ordering schedule (F1, invariant boundary = `writeProfile` settles):
```
  t | R1 (began before W)              | W                              | cache[k] | inflight[k]
  1 | get->undef; run(); DB read sent  |                                | -        | E1 stale=F
  2 |                                  | DB write commits V2            | -        | E1
  3 | DB returns V1 (resume queued)    |                                | -        | E1
  4 |                                  | resume: invalidate(E1), delete | -        | - (E1 detached)
  5 |                                  | settles -> W complete          | -        | -
  6 | resume: E1.stale -> skip fill    |                                | -        | -
    | return V1 (allowed: began < 5)   |                                |          |
  7 | R2 begins: miss, new E2, DB->V2, fill V2                          | V2  OK   | E2
  Order B (6 before 4): R1 fills V1, then W deletes at 4 -> R2 misses -> V2  OK
  Late joiner R3 arriving after 5: E1 detached -> new entry -> V2  OK
  Original sketch, order A: fill V1 at 6 after delete at 4 -> R2 reads V1 for <=30 s  VIOLATION
  Original sketch, R3 after 5: joins E1 -> V1  VIOLATION
```

Cache mode state machine:
```
  DISABLED ──flag on (empty cache)──▶ ENABLED ──adapter failure──▶ BYPASS
     ▲                                  │  ▲                          │
     └────────flag off──────────────────┘  └──flag toggle (reinit)────┘
  Any flag value change (incl. %) while ENABLED: flush -> ENABLED (empty)
  Invalid: BYPASS -> ENABLED without reinit (prevented: adapter only re-enables on init)
```

Error flow:
```
  repository error ──▶ typed API error (existing) ──▶ caller; no fill; entry released
  adapter error    ──▶ BYPASS + fallback metric + log(class) ──▶ caller unaffected ──▶ alert >5 min
  flag eval error  ──▶ bypass for that call + log ──▶ caller unaffected
  write error      ──▶ finally: invalidate + delete ──▶ typed error to caller
```

Deployment sequence:
```
  deploy code (flag off) ─▶ smoke (bypass path) ─▶ 10% keys ─▶ 1 h healthy ─▶ 50% ─▶ 1 h ─▶ 100%
  healthy = error rate in SLO, fallback errors 0, per-path p95 not worse, hits rising
```

Rollback flowchart:
```
  regression? ──yes──▶ flag off (seconds) ──▶ cache dropped ──▶ verify error rate/p95 ──▶ file defect
      │no                                                             │ still bad
      ▼                                                               ▼
  continue stage                                     revert deploy (not cache-related)
```

Test map:
```
  NEW UX FLOWS:            none
  NEW DATA FLOWS:          miss fill; negative fill; write invalidation; in-flight
                           invalidation; flag bucket routing; flag-change flush
  NEW CODEPATHS:           hit; miss+fill; miss+skip(stale); join in-flight; oversize skip;
                           adapter bypass; flag-disabled bypass
  NEW ASYNC WORK:          in-flight entry lifecycle (create, join, invalidate, release)
  NEW INTEGRATIONS:        none (flag SDK existing)
  NEW ERROR/RESCUE PATHS:  see Error & Rescue Registry
```
Assertions (unit unless noted): hit returns cached value without DB call; miss
calls DB once and fills; TTL expiry misses at 30 s (fake timers); 1001st entry
evicts one; byte cap evicts; oversize single value is not stored and mode stays
enabled; absent read stores sentinel, second read makes no DB call, expires at
10 s; write after absent clears sentinel; successful write leaves no entry;
rejected write leaves no entry (D5); ordering order A and order B both yield V2
for a post-write reader (D4); late joiner after write gets fresh read (D4);
sentinel variant of order A (D4); N concurrent misses make 1 DB call; adapter
`get` throw enters bypass, increments fallback metric, caller gets value;
adapter `delete` throw does not fail the write; read and write map a key to the
same bucket; disabled bucket makes no cache calls; percentage change flushes
(D9); flag evaluation error bypasses; mutating a returned DTO does not change
the next read; contract suite passes through warm wrapper (D6, integration);
metric labels and log lines match no ID pattern; trace replay of 900 hot keys
reaches >= 60% hits with per-path histograms (D7, load).
Friday-2am test: order A ordering test. Hostile QA: late joiner after write.
Chaos: adapter throws on every 3rd call, service stays correct in bypass.

### NOT in scope
- Distributed or cross-process cache: plan constraint; single process only.
- Prewarming: cold start fits existing DB capacity.
- Consistency semantics change: invariant retained as written.
- Capacity increase beyond 1000 entries / 16 MiB: hypothetical load, not evidenced.
- Auto-recovery from BYPASS without a flag toggle: alert plus runbook is adequate.
- Write-through (Approach C): marginal benefit, adds coupling.

### What already exists
LRU adapter (limits, TTL, sentinel, bypass) reused as-is; single-flight wrapper
reused with one added method; runtime flag reused; repository contract tests
reused and extended to the warm path; typed error mapping unchanged.

### Dream state delta
After this plan the service has a flag-gated, invariant-safe local cache behind
the unchanged repository interface. Remaining distance to the 12-month ideal is
only a swappable cache implementation, which the seam already permits.

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous
  misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.

## Proposed wrapper integration (amended)
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters. The
original sketch (invalidate-on-write only, "no additional version checks or
coordination between a cache fill and a write") violates the read-after-write
invariant above; see [F1]. The accepted ordering rules are:

```javascript
// Generation guard [F1]: a fill lands only if no write to the key completed
// between this read's cache miss and its DB result. Stamps come from one
// process-wide monotonic clock, so a stamp never repeats after eviction or
// reinit; a lost stamp can only cause a harmless skipped fill, never a stale one.
let writeClock = 0;                              // never reset
let writeGen = new BoundedMap(10_000);           // key -> stamp of last completed write attempt
const stamp = (key) => writeGen.get(key) ?? 0;

async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!inCohort(key)) return repository.read(key);           // [F3] shared deterministic cohort
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return fromCached(cached);          // [F2] ABSENT -> same absent result as repository
  const seen = stamp(key);
  const value = await singleFlight(`${key}#${seen}`,           // [F1] post-write readers never join a pre-commit flight
                                   () => repository.read(key));
  if (stamp(key) === seen) cache.set(key, toCached(value));     // [F2] absent -> ABSENT sentinel, 10 s TTL (adapter)
  else metrics.increment('profile_cache.fill_skipped_stale');   // [F1] skipped fill is visible, never silent
  return value;
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  let saved;
  try {
    saved = await repository.write(key, update);
  } finally {
    writeGen.set(key, ++writeClock);   // [F1] bump on success AND failure (a timed-out write may have committed)
  }
  cache.delete(key);                   // success only: failed-write preservation retained
  return saved;
}

// [F3] Any runtime flag change (percentage up, down, or off) reinitializes an
// empty cache and clears writeGen; writeClock is kept. Logged without keys.
flag.onChange((next) => { cache = adapter.createEmpty(); writeGen.clear();
  log.info('profile_cache.reinit', { reason: 'flag_change', cohort_pct: next.pct }); });
```

`toCached`/`fromCached` map the repository's absence signal to the adapter's
ABSENT sentinel and back, so a cached absence produces exactly the same caller
outcome as an uncached one [F2]. `inCohort(key)` is one deterministic hash
function used by both `readProfile` and `writeProfile` [F3].

## Verification and rollout (amended)
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. That same suite also runs against the
caching wrapper with the flag enabled, once cold and once pre-warmed [F6].
New wrapper tests cover hit/miss, eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure
fallback, successful-write invalidation, failed-write preservation,
concurrent-miss coalescing, controlled-schedule read/write interleavings [F1],
absent-sentinel behavior [F2], cohort membership and flag-change reinit [F3],

empty cache [F3]. Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The
service owner monitors the rollout and records the results against the
acceptance targets.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.
